about.title: About the portal
about.intro: Meteoportal is the official source of air quality and weather data for Tajikistan: measurements from the monitoring network, forecasts, warnings and health advice in three languages.

agency.title: Operator
agency.text: The Agency runs national ambient air monitoring and hydrometeorological observations and issues forecasts and severe weather warnings. The portal is its public data showcase.

project.title: FINTAJ project
project.text: The portal was developed within FINTAJ, the Finnish–Tajik cooperation project strengthening the hydrometeorological service of Tajikistan.
project.fmi: The donor and technical partner is the Finnish Meteorological Institute (FMI): weather forecasts come from SmartMet Server, the air quality forecast from the SILAM model, and warnings from the SmartMet Alert editor in CAP format.

sources.title: Where the data comes from
sources.intro: All external sources are synchronised in the background; if a source is unavailable the portal keeps showing the latest data marked as stale.

stations.title: Monitoring stations
stations.text: PM2.5, PM10, NO₂, SO₂, CO and O₃ concentrations from the Agency's stations: manual entry, imports and automatic sensors. Data passes quality control.

smartmet.title: Weather forecast
smartmet.text: SmartMet Server (FMI): hourly forecast for 3 days and daily forecast for 10 days for cities and districts.

silam.title: Air quality forecast
silam.text: SILAM chemical transport model (FMI): concentration maps and point forecasts for 5 days.

cap.title: Warnings
cap.text: SmartMet Alert messages in CAP 1.2: hazardous phenomena by region with yellow / orange / red levels.

openData.title: Open data
openData.text: Current and historical data is available through a JSON API, CSV exports and embeddable widgets.

languages.title: Languages and accessibility
languages.text: The portal is available in Tajik, Russian and English; the Tajik version is the primary one.

about.accessibility: The interface follows WCAG 2.1 AA: pollution levels are conveyed by colour and label, every action is keyboard-accessible, and dark mode and reduced motion are supported.

contacts.title: Contacts
contacts.none: Contact details will be published after approval by the Agency.

about.disclaimer: Data is published for information purposes. Official environmental statements are issued by the Agency.

aboutIndex.title: About the air quality index
aboutIndex.intro: How station measurements become five clear levels, which thresholds apply, and how the national index differs from the WHO scale.

operational.title: Operational five-level index

measure.title: Measurement
measure.text: For each pollutant the latest hourly mean is taken (8-hour mean for CO). Only measurements that passed quality control are used.

subindex.title: Pollutant sub-index
subindex.text: The value is compared with the threshold table and gets a level from 1 (good) to 5 (very poor). The position within the band is kept, so the index can also be shown as a number.

max.title: Station index
max.text: The station index is the worst sub-index. The pollutant with the highest sub-index is called dominant and is shown next to the level.

operational.note: This approach is used by operational indices in Europe (for example FMI/HSY): it shows the current situation without smoothing peaks. The thresholds below are edited by the Agency without a software release.

aboutIndex.thresholdsCaption: Concentration thresholds by pollutant and level
aboutIndex.thresholdsHint: Intervals are half-open: the lower bound is included, the upper is not. Units are µg/m³; mg/m³ for CO.
aboutIndex.noScale: The scale has not been configured yet.

colors.title: How to read the colours
colors.level2: Acceptable quality; very sensitive people may notice slight discomfort.
colors.level3: Sensitive groups should reduce prolonged outdoor exertion.
colors.level4: Pollution is noticeable for everyone: limit time outdoors, especially for children and the elderly.
colors.level5: Very high pollution: stay indoors if possible and keep windows closed.
colors.level6: Hazardous (sixth level of scales such as the US AQI): extremely high pollution — everyone should stay indoors and avoid physical activity outside.
colors.level0: No data, or the data is stale (measurement older than 6 hours).
colors.accessibility: Colour is never the only carrier of meaning: a level label is always shown next to it and a number on the map. Colours are chosen for a text contrast of at least 4.5:1 in light and dark themes.

national.title: National index: ratio to limit values and the IZA
national.ratio: The ratio to limit value compares a concentration with the maximum permissible concentration (MPC): the daily mean with the daily MPC, the maximum single value with the single MPC. Up to 1 means the standard is met; levels 2–5 correspond to ratios of 1–2, 2–3, 3–5 and above 5.
national.iza: The composite air pollution index (IZA, RD 52.04.186-89) sums normalised monthly mean concentrations of the five pollutants with the largest contribution, weighted by hazard class: IZA = Σ (q̄ᵢ / MPCᵢ)^Cᵢ. Grades: low < 5, elevated 5–6, high 7–13, very high ≥ 14.
national.note: Limit values and hazard classes are tabular data of the Agency for Hydrometeorology (daily air pollution bulletins, limits in mg/m³) and are edited in the admin panel.

who.title: WHO guideline scale
who.text: An optional scale based on the WHO Air Quality Guidelines 2021 and interim targets (24-hour means). Available in the API with scale=WHO_24H.

quality.title: Data quality
quality.text: Every measurement is checked: physical range, spikes, stuck sensors and outliers relative to the station's history. Suspect values are reviewed by an operator; only valid and corrected values are published.
quality.stale: If the measurement is older than 6 hours the index is considered stale and shown as grey “no data” — an honest gap is better than an outdated number.

agency.title: Agency for Hydrometeorology method
agency.intro: The Agency's daily air pollution bulletins assess air quality by the ratio of concentrations to maximum permissible concentrations (MPC). The portal calculates the same indicators from the valid measurements of each station (the “Ratio to limit values” scale, scale=RATIO_TO_LIMIT in the API).

ratio.title: Ratio to MPC
ratio.text: The daily mean concentration is divided by the daily MPC and the maximum single value of the day by the single MPC. A ratio up to 1 means the standard is met; the scale levels correspond to ratios up to 1, 1–2, 2–3, 3–5 and above 5.

sum.title: NO₂ + SO₂ summation
sum.text: Nitrogen dioxide and sulphur dioxide have a summation effect: their daily-MPC ratios are added and the sum should not exceed 1. The indicator is calculated when the station measures both pollutants.

cases.title: High and extremely high pollution
cases.text: High pollution (HP) means the maximum single concentration reached 10 single MPCs, extremely high pollution (EHP) — 50 single MPCs. The flags are shown on the station page and returned by the API.

agency.compare: Bulletins assess the change against the previous day; on the portal the measurement chart shows the dynamics, and the ratios are recalculated every 10 minutes over a sliding 24-hour window.
agency.units: Bulletins publish concentrations in mg/m³; the display unit of the portal (µg/m³ or mg/m³) is chosen by the administrator, and the API and CSV state the unit in the unit field.

data.title: Open data
data.intro: Measurements, the index, forecasts and warnings are available in machine-readable form — for researchers, the media, app developers and the meteo.tj website.
data.csvHint: Add format=csv to download a table

formats.title: Formats
formats.json: JSON — the primary format of all endpoints
formats.csv: CSV (UTF-8 with BOM) — measurement series for spreadsheets and analysis
formats.xml: CAP XML and RSS 2.0 — warnings and news

widgets.title: Widgets for websites
widgets.text: Ready-made iframe blocks: station index, weather forecast, warnings. The language is set with the lang parameter.

data.quality: Station data is published after automatic and manual quality control; values marked “stale” or “no data” mean a gap, not zero pollution.

apiDocs.title: API for developers
apiDocs.intro: Public REST API version 1: reads without keys, JSON by default; station data intake — POST with a station key. The OpenAPI 3.1 specification is generated from the same schemas that validate server requests and responses.
apiDocs.authHint: Not required for reads (limit 120 requests per minute per IP). Station data intake: Authorization: Bearer <station key> header, separate limit of 60 requests per minute per station.
apiDocs.corsHint: Requests from any website are allowed (Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *).

responses.csv: CSV (UTF-8 with BOM): time_utc, time_local, pollutant, value, min, max, n
responses.ingestOk: At least one record accepted (reasons for rejected ones in errors)
responses.unauthorized: Missing Authorization header or the key does not match the station code

apiDocs.licenseNote: Data is licensed under CC BY 4.0 with attribution; FMI forecasts must credit the Finnish Meteorological Institute.
apiDocs.embedNote: For websites without development there are iframe widgets /embed/aqi, /embed/forecast and /embed/alerts (see Open data).

info.title: Meteoportal of Tajikistan — public API
info.description: Air quality, weather and air quality forecasts, CAP warnings and news of the Agency for Hydrometeorology of the Republic of Tajikistan. Times are UTC (ISO 8601); local time is Asia/Dushanbe (UTC+5).

stations.description: Public stations (except decommissioned) as a GeoJSON FeatureCollection with the current index level; 0 means no data or stale.

stationMeasurements.description: Hourly (24h, 7d) or daily local-time (30d, 1y) means of valid measurements with min/max and count. CSV with format=csv. Values and the unit field use the display unit chosen by the Agency (µg/m³ or mg/m³).

params.slug: Station address (the slug field from the station list)
params.pollutant: Pollutant code (PM25, PM10, NO2, SO2, CO, O3, NO, CH2O, C6H5OH, HF, TSP, CO2, TVOC); all pollutants when omitted

indexCurrent.description: The latest computed index of every public station: level, value, dominant pollutant, sub-indices and a stale flag (older than 6 hours). For the RATIO_TO_LIMIT scale the response includes the Agency method indicators: NO₂+SO₂ summation, maximum single concentrations with the ratio to the single MPC, high/extremely high pollution flags; units — display units per pollutant.

params.scale: Scale code: NATIONAL_OPERATIONAL (default), WHO_24H or IZA

exceedances.description: Open exceedance events according to the Agency's alert rules (portal channel).

forecast.description: Hourly series and daily aggregates from SmartMet Server; model run time and data producer.

params.hours: Number of hours in the hourly series (1–240)
params.days: Number of days in the daily forecast (1–16)

silamPoint.summary: SILAM air quality forecast for a location
silamPoint.description: Hourly concentrations and levels by pollutant plus a daily summary (local-day mean, level by the worst pollutant).

silamLayers.description: Grid bounds and PNG frames by pollutant and hour of the latest run — for map overlays.

alerts.description: Normalised list of SmartMet Alert warnings in the selected language (with fallback) or GeoJSON polygons for maps.

params.region: Warning region code (DU, SU, KT, GB, RRP)
params.lang: Text language: tg, ru or en

news.description: Published news with excerpt, category, cover and page link.

newsRss.description: The 20 latest news items as RSS 2.0 in the selected language.

regions.description: Regions, Dushanbe and the RRP with simplified polygons, centroids, station counts and the worst current index level (0 — no data). Cached for 10 minutes, ETag.

districts.description: Districts and cities of regional subordination with simplified polygons, region code, station counts and the worst current index level. Units without loaded geometry are omitted.

ingest.description: A logger, the station agent or vendor software sends a JSON array of measurements (up to 1000 per request). Time — ISO 8601 with offset or local (Asia/Dushanbe); pollutants — codes PM25, PM10, NO2, SO2, CO, O3 or synonyms; the default unit is the station's input unit. Values are converted to the pollutant unit, pass the QC range rule and are stored by the time/pollutant/averaging key — re-sending is idempotent and operator decisions are kept. The response lists accepted and rejected counts with per-record reasons. After storing, the index and alert rules are recomputed.

params.code: Station code from the registry (e.g. DU-01)

security.stationApiKey: Station API key from the station card in the admin panel; sent as Authorization: Bearer <key>. Only the key hash is stored in the database.

ecoBulletin.title: Eco-bulletin
ecoBulletin.subtitle: Daily ecological bulletin in the Agency's format: city table and text, cities summary (ЗАВ / ИҲА), form 4a

form.title: New bulletin
form.hint: Computed from valid measurements of the local day (Asia/Dushanbe); compared with the previous day. The cities summary covers all public stations.

fields.author: Author
fields.gammaHint: Manual entry, e.g. 0,014; leave empty to omit the gamma paragraph

docs.cityHint: Ecological bulletin / Шарҳи ҳолати ифлосшавии ҳаво
docs.summaryHint: Air pollution in the cities / ИҲА

ecoBulletin.pdfHint: PDF is rendered by Chromium on the server; if unavailable, a print version opens — save it as PDF from the print dialog
ecoBulletin.publishConfirm: Documents (DOCX, PDF when Chromium is available) are stored in the portal archive “Eco-bulletins” and a published news post with attachments is created. A published bulletin cannot be changed.

warnings.noData: No valid measurements for the station on the selected day — the table is empty
warnings.noYesterday: No data for the previous day — the day-to-day comparison was skipped

settings.title: Eco-bulletin settings
settings.hint: Draft schedule, notifications, signature and the exceedance causes phrase. Other wording lives in the template file packages/core/src/bulletin-phrases.ts.
settings.schedule: Prepare a draft daily at 08:00 (Dushanbe) for the previous day
settings.notify: E-mail operators and administrators when a draft is ready
settings.stationsHint: Empty — all public stations with continuous measurements
settings.departmentHint: Empty — from the template (ОИ УМОС / ШИ РММЗ)
settings.causesHint: Inserted into the sentence about exceedance cases; empty — from the template
settings.summationMaxSingle: relative to the max single limit — Agency method (0,66 in the sample)
settings.summationDaily: relative to the daily limit — summation rule of RD 52.04.186-89

public.title: Ecological bulletins
public.intro: Daily ecological bulletins of the Agency for Hydrometeorology: air pollution in the cities of the republic for the previous day
public.languageNote: The documents are issued in Tajik and Russian.

errors.locked: A published bulletin cannot be changed
errors.noData: No valid measurements for the station on the selected day
errors.future: The date cannot be later than today

news.title: Ecological bulletin of {city} for {date}
news.excerpt: Air pollution in {city} and the cities of the republic for {date}

pollutantHints.PM25: PM2.5 — fine particulate matter (up to 2.5 µm): smoke, exhaust, soot
pollutantHints.PM10: PM10 — dust, coarse particulate matter (up to 10 µm)
pollutantHints.NO2: NO₂ — nitrogen dioxide: vehicle exhaust, boilers
pollutantHints.SO2: SO₂ — sulphur dioxide: burning coal and fuel oil
pollutantHints.CO: CO — carbon monoxide: incomplete fuel combustion
pollutantHints.O3: O₃ — ground-level ozone: forms in hot sunny weather
pollutantHints.NO: NO — nitric oxide: exhaust and industry
pollutantHints.TSP: TSP — total suspended particles of all sizes
pollutantHints.CO2: CO₂ — carbon dioxide: an indicator of ventilation
pollutantHints.TVOC: TVOC — volatile organic compounds: solvents, fuel
